title: Sustainable Regional Dispatcher with Integrated Circuit-Breaker Fabric and Elastic Shedding Lanes
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: During periodic regional capacity degradation and large traffic surges we need a single coherent dispatch layer that meets customer latency SLOs, preserves affinity where beneficial, and degrades predictably. Current behavior routes purely by proximity or static weights which causes cascades when one region enters a slow path. This epic creates a ‘Sustainable Regional Dispatcher’ that blends latency-aware decisioning, geo affinity heuristics, and capacity-aware shedding via an integrated circuit-breaker fabric.

Goals: 1) Keep 95th percentile request latency under per-customer SLOs for hosted API traffic by preferring local/near regions when available. 2) Prevent cross-region overload amplification and global tail latency spikes via graded circuit breakers. 3) Provide transparent fallbacks, observable decisions, and per-tenant opt-outs (pinning). 4) Enable safe rollouts with canary traffic shaping and console-level controls.

Scope: Design and implement control plane policies and runtime hooks for scoring destinations on latency, healthy capacity headroom, and affinity score; implement circuit-breaker fabric that emits reasoned reject/failover vs. shed decisions; extend console to surface routing decisions, per-region capacity signals, and a simple troubleshooting playbook. Integration points include request director, autoscaler events, per-region metrics pipeline, and the KV cache awareness layer to avoid inefficient cross-region cache-miss amplification.
acceptance_criteria: Dispatcher computes an ordered candidate list for each request combining measured p50/p95 latency, recent capacity headroom, and affinity score.
Reactive circuit-breaker fabric trips per-region with at least three configurable thresholds (soft-degrade, hard-degrade, evict) and emits structured reasons in traces and logs.

Load-shedding lanes implement graceful degradation: 1) prefer compressed/quantized model variant; 2) fallback to limited token budget; 3) finally reject with structured error and suggested retry-after header.
Per-tenant geo-pinning honor set and override semantics (sticky for X minutes; manual override via Console + API).
End-to-end e2e tests that simulate region slowdowns produce predictable fallback decisions without exceeding configured global error budget.
Console shows per-route decision breakdown for at least 90% of sampled traffic and a new dashboard for regional admission and breaker state.
implementation_notes: Scoring function: score = w_latency * normalized_latency + w_headroom * (1 - normalized_headroom) + w_affinity * (1 - affinity_penalty). Tunable weights per route and tenant.
Latency signals: combine real-time p50/p95 from CDN/gateway latencies with recent request quantiles from region telemetry (10s sliding window).
Capacity headroom: use autoscaler-backed tokens + instantaneous GPU queue depth as two signals; headroom normalized to 0..1.

Circuit-breaker tiers: soft-degrade -> reduce allowed concurrent requests and prefer skinny model; hard-degrade -> route to remote region with capacity; evict -> shed best-effort non-critical requests and surface 429 with retry-after.
KV cache awareness: prefer destinations with warm KV hit ratios for the request hash to avoid massive cold-KV cross-region traffic.
Data retention: breaker events and decision traces need 7 days hot retention for debugging; aggregated 30d for trend analysis.
APIs: add /dispatch/explain for sampled requests returning ordered candidate list and reason codes (for internal use and Console diagnostic panes).
rollout_plan: Week 1: Implement scoring module and experiment in dev cluster behind feature flag. Add metric hooks and tracing annotations.
Week 2: Canary in staging with 1% of traffic; validate decision correctness with synthetic region slowdowns and capacity constraints.
Week 3: Gradual rollout to 10% then 25% traffic in production, monitor SLOs and breaker churn; enable per-tenant opt-in lists.
Week 4: Full rollout for non-reserved hosted plans; hold dedicated capacity customers behind opt-in until acceptance review.
Mitigation: feature flagging allows immediate global disable. Provide operator playbook to drain and revert via Console.
